fish.name: Lamplight Minnow
fish.flavor: Schools beneath the streetlamps after dark, wearing the reflections like tiny coats. Turns off, somehow, when the lamps do.

fish.name: Ha'penny Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Copper-scaled and terribly proud of it. Worth roughly half of what it believes it is, which is still more than most gudgeon.

fish.name: Mooring Sprat
fish.flavor: Ties itself to dock posts with knots no sailor can name. Untying one voids the warranty, whatever that means.

fish.name: Cobble Dab
fish.flavor: Flat, round, and gray as the harbor road. Street pavers occasionally install one by accident, and it never complains.

fish.name: Gutterling
fish.flavor: A soft, damp little optimist that rides the rain down the drainspouts and calls it travel. Collects bottle caps for luck.

fish.name: Bollard Bream
fish.flavor: Squat, sturdy, and immovable once it has decided on a spot. Ferries have learned to steer around it.

fish.name: Teacup Tiddler
fish.flavor: Precisely one teacup in volume, no more, no less. Harbor grannies leave chipped cups on the seawall just for them.

fish.name: Ropecoil Eel
fish.flavor: Sleeps coiled on the dock in a perfect figure-eight, and more than one deckhand has tried to stow it. It bites, politely.

fish.name: Fog Smelt
fish.flavor: Arrives with the morning fog and leaves with it too. Catch one and your hands smell faintly of weather.

fish.name: Bellwether Herring
fish.flavor: Swims upside down exactly one hour before rain. The harbormaster trusts it more than the almanac, and says so loudly.

fish.name: Parcel Perch
fish.flavor: Banded like brown paper and string, and forever swimming somewhere with great purpose. Return to sender if found.

fish.name: Umbrella Guppy
fish.flavor: Unfurls its frills at the first drop of rain and glides about looking tremendously prepared. Folds them, smugly, when it stops.

fish.name: Soot Mudskip
fish.flavor: Blackened from naps in the ferry exhaust, which it swears are good for the constitution. Leaves little footprints on the pier.

fish.name: Wharfcat Whisker
fish.flavor: Prowls the pilings at night and purrs when you scratch under its chin. The harbor cats regard it as one of their own.

fish.name: Clocktower Carp
fish.flavor: Surfaces at noon precisely, every day, to check the clocktower against its own opinion. It has been correcting the clock since 1874.

fish.name: Left-Shoe Sole
fish.flavor: Shaped exactly like a left shoe, always a left. Where the rights go is one of the harbor's oldest and most carefully unasked questions.

fish.name: Gossip Grayling
fish.flavor: Blows bubbles that pop with fragments of conversations overheard on the pier. Nothing scandalous yet, but it is clearly waiting.

fish.name: Milk-Eye Mullet
fish.flavor: Its pale eyes see nothing in this world, which locals say is because they are busy with another one. Perfectly friendly. Probably.

fish.name: Buttonspot Loach
fish.flavor: Dotted with markings shaped like coat buttons, no two sets alike. Tailors check the canals every spring for new patterns.

fish.name: Marionette Pike
fish.flavor: Moves in sharp little jerks, as if worked by strings from somewhere above the water. Anglers who look up report seeing nothing, twice.

fish.name: Widdershins Wrasse
fish.flavor: Only ever swims counterclockwise, even when it would be much faster not to. Turning one around is considered very bad manners.

fish.name: Manhole Ray
fish.flavor: Round, iron-gray, and stamped with a pattern suspiciously like the city seal. Occasionally the road crew bolts one down by mistake.

fish.name: Pocketwatch Puffer
fish.flavor: Inflates on the hour with a soft, dignified tick. Runs four minutes slow, exactly like the gentleman who lost it.

fish.name: Ferryman's Toll
fish.flavor: A flat, pale fish stamped like an old coin, found only where the last ferry crosses at night. Keep it, and something considers the fare paid.

fish.name: Mirrorscale Wanderer
fish.flavor: Its scales reflect the harbor perfectly, except the buildings are wrong and the lamps burn green. Nobody has found that harbor yet.

fish.name: Doppelgudgeon
fish.flavor: Takes the shape of the last fish you caught, down to the guilty expression. In a bare bucket it simply sulks, shapeless and offended.

fish.name: Whistling Moray
fish.flavor: Lives in the storm drains and whistles shanties through them on windy nights. Takes requests, but only sad ones.

fish.name: Pinstripe Prowler
fish.flavor: A small shark in a very sharp suit of stripes, running the canals like it owns them. Rumor says the pilings pay it protection in barnacles.

fish.name: Quillfin Scrivener
fish.flavor: Writes in the silt with its long inked snout, always the same phrase: WITNESSED AND RECORDED. Nobody knows for whom.

fish.name: The Harbormaster's Regret
fish.flavor: A gray-green fish that circles the oldest pier once a year, on the anniversary of a promise nobody kept. It looks at you like it knows which one was yours.

fish.name: Foglantern Seiner
fish.flavor: Carries a lure of cold amber light and drifts through the thickest harbor fog, gathering lost things into its glow. Sailors follow it home; the wise ones stop at the dock.

fish.name: Saint Elmo's Herald
fish.flavor: Arrives ahead of the big storms, crackling faintly, scales lit like mast-fire. Every lighthouse keeper on the coast owes it at least one apology.

fish.name: The Drowned Bellringer
fish.flavor: When the old church slid into the harbor, they say the bell kept ringing. It did — it just grew fins, and it has kept every midnight since. You feel the toll in your teeth before you hear it.

fish.name: Grandmother Undertow
fish.flavor: The oldest thing in the canals, coiled under the city like a rumor. She remembers when the harbor was a meadow, and if you are very polite, she will tell you what it will be next.

fish.name: The City Beneath
fish.flavor: A ray the size of a plaza, its back tiled with rooftops, lit windows, and streetlamps that come on at dusk. Look long enough and you will find your own house among them, with someone waving from the door.
